soft_event_news.title: What Oracle Layoffs Mean for ORCL Stock Now - MEXC Exchange
soft_event_news.body:
Oracle is back in focus as layoffs and AI spending collide. The company is reportedly cutting thousands of jobs while trying to control rising data-center costs tied to its aggressive cloud and AI buildout, and the move has turned ORCL into a stock investors are watching closely. That has raised a simple question: are the layoffs a warning sign, or a cost reset that could help Oracle protect margins and regain confidence?

Oracle is back in focus as layoffs and AI spending collide. The company is reportedly cutting thousands of jobs while trying to control rising data-center costs tied to its aggressive cloud and AI buildout, and the move has turned ORCL into a stock investors are watching closely. That has raised a simple question: are the layoffs a warning sign, or a cost reset that could help Oracle protect margins and regain confidence?

The stock itself has been under pressure. ORCL closed at $138.80 on March 30, after a recent stretch that saw shares fall from $155.52 on March 19 to $138.80 by the end of the month, according to historical price data. That drop came even after Oracle reported stronger-than-expected fiscal third-quarter results earlier in March, including 22% year-over-year revenue growth and adjusted EPS of $1.79.

The layoff story matters because it sits at the center of Oracle’s bigger AI strategy. Reuters reported that the cuts could hit multiple divisions as the company absorbs the cost of its data-center expansion, while other reports said Oracle has also been slowing hiring in cloud-related areas. In other words, the company is still pushing into AI infrastructure, but it appears to be tightening spending at the same time.

The chart pattern is still weak in the short term. ORCL has slipped below the mid-March support area near $150 and is trying to stabilize closer to $140, which makes that zone the first level bulls need to defend. A move back above $145 would be an early sign that sellers are losing momentum. If the stock cannot hold the low-$140s, traders may continue to treat rallies as short-term bounces rather than the start of a clean reversal.

For momentum traders, layoffs are not just a headline; they can also be read as a cost-cutting catalyst. If Oracle uses workforce reductions to improve cash flow while keeping cloud growth intact, the market may eventually reward the move.

But if investors see the cuts as proof that AI spending is getting too expensive, the stock could stay under pressure. Right now, ORCL is caught between a growth story and a margin story, and the chart suggests the market wants clearer evidence before paying up again.
